answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bonded identity registry: to hold one voice an agent must lock its own stake, bound to a single cryptographic identity. A farmer then pays one fresh deposit per fake agent, so a thousand votes cost a thousand bonds. Random audits slash the whole bond of anyone caught signing two names, and a nullifier stops reusing one deposit. The shared harbor is thus costly to flood, its rules hard as quartz, and any collusive vine is cheap to cut.
